## Learning Outcomes

By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

- Explain what the IMAG simulation measures and why AuM matters
- Describe the fund, client, benchmark and portfolio structure
- Navigate the four-station allocation app alongside the Cesim Invest platform
- Follow the eight-step decision flow from client information to round results
- Organise your team workflow and governance for practice and scored rounds

# The Firm, the Funds, the Clients {background-color="#1e3a5f"}

## Asterion Capital

- You are a fund manager at **Asterion Capital**, whose founders are stepping back
- The firm runs up to four funds, one per client type:
  - **Conservative**
  - **Conservative (ESG)**
  - **Dynamic**
  - **Dynamic (ESG)**
- Each fund has its own clients, its own benchmark and its own fee structure

## What Stays Fixed vs. What Changes?

- **Fixed for the entire game:**
  - The client profile and fund type
  - The client's home market, investment rules and guidance bands (on the **Clients** page)
  - The strategic asset allocation (**SAA**), set in Round 1 as the fund's benchmark
- **Updated every round:**
  - Economic views and the tactical asset allocation (**TAA**)
  - Optional security-level adjustments
  - Management fees (charged on Assets under Management, **AuM**)

# The Portfolio Universe {background-color="#1e3a5f"}

## 180 Assets, 21 Positions, 16 Benchmark Segments

| Asset Class | USD | GBP | EUR | CHF | JPY | In SAA Benchmark? |
|:--|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--|
| **Money market** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | **No** (5 tactical cash positions) |
| **Government bonds** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | **Yes** (5 benchmark positions) |
| **Corporate bonds** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | **Yes** (5 benchmark positions) |
| **Equities** | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | **Yes** (5 benchmark positions) |
| **Alternatives (Commodities)** | ✓ | — | — | — | — | **Yes** (1 USD position) |
: {tbl-colwidths="[28,8,8,8,8,8,32]"}

- **21 total positions** across the 5 currencies; the **SAA benchmark** is defined on the **16 non-cash segments**.

## The Dollar Numeraire & Currency Risk

- Asterion measures everything in **US dollars (USD)**
- Foreign-currency assets are held **unhedged** — the game offers no currency hedging instruments
- Every non-USD position therefore combines **local asset risk + FX risk against the dollar**
- The optimal strategic benchmark holds **no cash**: holding cash is an active tactical decision, not a strategic position

# What the Game Measures {background-color="#1e3a5f"}

## Three Channels Drive AuM

AuM is the capital a fund manages. Since each fund earns its percentage management fee on its AuM, **growing AuM drives the firm's profit**. AuM responds to three channels:

1. **Risk-Adjusted Performance against the Benchmark**
2. **Client Satisfaction**
3. **Management Fees**

## 1. Risk-Adjusted Performance

- Measured against each fund's own **strategic allocation (SAA)**
- Raw return alone does not win the game; risk-adjusted and benchmark-relative metrics matter
- The **Analyst** page decomposes and attributes returns by:
  - Currency and asset class (allocation effect)
  - Industry, maturity and factor exposures (selection effect)
  - Comparison of your SAA against the game's hidden optimal allocation for the client

## 2. Client Satisfaction

- Client surveys evaluate whether the fund is managed as promised on the **Clients** page:
  - Staying inside the client's **guidance bands** and hard limits
  - Taking the level of risk consistent with the client's risk aversion ($\gamma$)
  - Meeting the required **ESG rating floor** for sustainability funds
- A fund held far from client expectations (e.g. parking a dynamic client in cash) loses clients immediately

## 3. Management Fees

- Quoted as an annual percentage on the **Clients** page (one quarter is charged per quarterly round)
- Higher fees increase revenue per dollar of AuM, but drive clients away
- Clients tolerate fees better when risk-adjusted performance is strong:
  - **Dynamic clients** respond to marketing and accept higher fees
  - **Conservative clients** demand low, transparent fees

## The Winning Criterion

Grow AuM and firm value by balancing all three channels:

1. Deliver strong **risk-adjusted performance** relative to the benchmark
2. Keep **clients satisfied** by respecting their mandate and risk profile
3. Charge an **appropriate fee** for each client segment

The instructor sets the final scoring metric (*Sharpe ratio, alpha, information ratio, or cumulative shareholder return*), all of which flow through these three channels.

# The Decision Flow & Allocation App {background-color="#1e3a5f"}

## Setup Once in Round 1 (Steps 1–3)

| Step | Page in the Game | What You Decide | Tool | Ch. |
|:--:|:--|:--|:--|:--:|
| **1** | Clients | Read client rules, $\gamma$ bracket & guidance bands | Client card | 2 |
| **2** | Course dataset | Inspect historical market statistics & correlations | App St. 1 | 3 |
| **3** | Strategy → Strategic allocation | Set and fix each fund's SAA benchmark | App St. 2 | 4 |
: {tbl-colwidths="[8,28,42,14,8]"}

- **Done once in Round 1:** the client profile does not change, and the SAA stays fixed as the fund's benchmark for the entire game
- **The Allocation App (<https://inno.uni.li/apps/invest/>):** runs on the full monthly USD course dataset; you compute matrices in the app and type them into the game grids

## Repeat Every Round (Steps 4–8)

| Step | Page in the Game | What You Decide | Tool | Ch. |
|:--:|:--|:--|:--|:--:|
| **4** | Economic outlook, Analyst | Turn macro outlook into expected-return views | App St. 3 | 5 |
| **5** | Strategy → Tactical allocation | Optimise this round's tactical weights (TAA) | App St. 4 | 6 |
| **6** | Strategy → Automation, Markets | Set ESG floor; decide on security selection | Game | 7 |
| **7** | Clients → Fees, Projections | Set fees, verify projections, submit Team Area | Game | 8 |
| **8** | Results, Analyst | Diagnose ratios, attribution & satisfaction | Game | 9 |
: {tbl-colwidths="[8,28,42,14,8]"}

- **Repeated every quarter:** form views from the new outlook, tilt the TAA via Black–Litterman, check automation/fees/projections, submit, and feed attribution back into the next round

# Rounds, Practice and Teams {background-color="#1e3a5f"}

## Practice Rounds vs. Scored Rounds

- A round typically represents **one quarter**
- The instructor may run up to **three practice rounds** before Round 1:
  - Practice results do not carry over; use them to master the platform and app workflow
  - After practice, the market resets and **Round 1 starts from the decisions of the first practice round**
- Between rounds, holdings drift with market returns and fund flows:
  - If automation is on, the game rebalances holdings back to your tactical weights
  - The SAA is never touched by market drift — it is a fixed benchmark, not a holding

## Student Area vs. Team Decision Area

- Every team member has a personal **Student Decision Area**
- Only the **Team Decision Area** is scored at the round deadline
- Workflow discipline:
  - Prepare and test decisions in your Student Decision Area
  - Compare team members' proposals side-by-side on the **Decision checklist** page
  - Click **Copy as team's decisions** only after agreeing (overwrites the Team Area without backup!)
  - Appoint a rotating **Round CEO** responsible for the final check and submission

## The Round on One Page

1. **Round 1 only:** Read the client (Ch. 2) and market (Ch. 3); optimise and fix the SAA for every fund (Ch. 4)
2. Set the **ESG rating floor** for ESG funds in *Automation preferences* (Ch. 7)
3. Read the *Economic outlook* and record views with confidence levels (Ch. 5)
4. Run Station 4 for every fund; enter the TAA and check projected tracking error & IR (Ch. 6)
5. Keep asset-level automation on in early rounds (or document specific security theses, Ch. 7)
6. Set fees, verify *Projections*, and copy to the **Team Decision Area** before the deadline (Ch. 8)
7. After the deadline: diagnose *Results* and *Analyst*; revise $\gamma$ (if needed once) and views (Ch. 9)

## Simulation Task — Lesson 1

::: {.callout-important}
## Deliverable: Platform, App & Team Setup

1. **Explore Cesim Invest:** Locate *Clients, Economic outlook, Investment strategy, Markets, Analyst, Decision checklist,* and *Projections*.
2. **Test the Allocation App:** Open <https://inno.uni.li/apps/invest/> and verify access to Stations 1–4.
3. **Establish Team Governance:** Appoint your Round 1 CEO, set an internal review deadline before copying to the *Team Decision Area*, and start your **team forum** log.
4. **Inspect Active Funds:** Check which of the four funds (*Conservative, Conservative ESG, Dynamic, Dynamic ESG*) are active in your game.
:::

## Key Takeaways

- Your **SAA is the fixed benchmark**; your **TAA and holdings** deviate tactically when justified by views
- **AuM** drives firm profit and responds to benchmark-relative performance, client satisfaction and fees
- Every foreign position is **unhedged in USD**, making currency risk an integral part of portfolio management
- Work in your **Student Decision Area**, log your reasoning in the forum, and copy deliberately to the **Team Decision Area**
